newsitem.title: UK: S&P sees more global reinsurance consolidation.
newsitem.headline: S&P sees more global reinsurance consolidation.

text.p: The global reinsurance industry will be the subject of further mergers and acquisitions, ratings agency Standard & Poor's said in its Global Reinsurance Highlights 1996 review.

"Consolidation is expected to continue on a rapid pace, as less secure market players or those owned by financial investors are combined with complementary strategic partners to diversify books of business, enhance market position and realise expense economies of scale," it said.
The review includes a survey of the world's leading reinsurers and articles on a number of reinsurance topics written by S&P directors and staff.
Margins have come under pressure from growing competition, "leaving little cushion for 'abnormal' losses from large catastrophes or adverse casualty reserve development," the review said.

The survivors will comprise companies with a competitive edge or a market niche, while smaller and weaker players will seek stronger partners or withdraw from the market altogether, S&P said. "Even top tier players in the (European) market are likely to show some deterioration in financial strength but are expected to preserve excellent capitalisation...those who possess more delicate financial health will find their lives S&P estimates that full year 1995 technical results for European reinsurers were similar to 1994, but added that underlying trends may vary from one region to another.
"Whether the future can also produce satisfactory profitability will in part depend on the discipline of primary writers and reinsurers around the world," it said.
Other factors affecting profitability include changes in capacity from markets such as Lloyd's and Bermuda and "the invariably fickle behaviour of Mother Nature," S&P added.
